semantic_correction.stem: A 52-year-old adult who has never received a pneumococcal conjugate vaccine asks about pneumococcal vaccination. Which response by the nurse is accurate according to current CDC recommendations?

options.A: Routine pneumococcal vaccination now applies at age 52; CDC recommends PCV15, PCV20, or PCV21, and if PCV15 is used, PPSV23 is given one year later.
options.B: Routine pneumococcal vaccination should wait until age 65 unless a new medical risk factor develops, because adults ages 50 through 64 are not included in the age-based recommendation.
options.C: At age 52, PPSV23 alone is the routine first choice and pneumococcal conjugate vaccination is deferred until age 65, regardless of previous conjugate-vaccine history.
options.D: Pneumococcal vaccination is generally started after a documented episode of pneumococcal pneumonia, rather than being recommended preventively on the basis of age.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. CDC guidance updated February 25, 2026 recommends routine pneumococcal vaccination for all adults age 50 years or older who have never received a pneumococcal conjugate vaccine or whose prior vaccination history is unknown. CDC recommends PCV15, PCV20, or PCV21 for this group; if PCV15 is used, PPSV23 is recommended one year later, whereas PCV20 or PCV21 completes the pneumococcal vaccination series without PPSV23. B is incorrect because the current age-based recommendation begins at age 50, not 65. C is incorrect because current CDC guidance begins with an indicated pneumococcal conjugate vaccine rather than PPSV23 alone for a PCV-naive 52-year-old. D is incorrect because vaccination is preventive and is routinely recommended by age; a prior episode of pneumococcal pneumonia is not required. CDC also notes that individual pneumococcal vaccines protect against different pneumococcal serotypes, so vaccination should not be described as preventing every possible cause of pneumonia.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Apply current CDC adult pneumococcal guidance by recognizing routine vaccination beginning at age 50 and selecting the appropriate conjugate-vaccine pathway for a PCV-naive adult.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Updated February 25, 2026; current CDC page accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Key points: CDC recommends pneumococcal vaccination for adults 50 years or older. Background: each individual pneumococcal vaccine protects against different serotypes of pneumococcal bacteria. 'Adults 50 years or older' → Routine vaccination recommendations: administer PCV15, PCV20, or PCV21 for all adults 50 years or older who have never received any pneumococcal conjugate vaccine or whose previous vaccination history is unknown. 'PCV15: Additional vaccination recommended': if PCV15 is used, administer one dose of PPSV23 one year later. 'PCV20 or PCV21: Additional vaccination not recommended': if PCV20 or PCV21 is used, PPSV23 is not indicated and pneumococcal vaccination is complete.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests the current age-50 pneumococcal recommendation and product pathway for a PCV-naive adult with one clearly best answer and no conspicuous cueing.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches the current CDC age threshold, PCV options, and the directly stated PCV15-to-PPSV23 sequence.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. It uses the outdated age-65 threshold and excludes adults age 50 through 64 from the current routine recommendation.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Current CDC guidance recommends an indicated PCV for this PCV-naive adult rather than PPSV23 alone as the routine initial pathway.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Pneumococcal vaccination is preventive and age-based; prior pneumococcal pneumonia is not a prerequisite.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone matches current CDC guidance for this exact age and vaccination history; B uses an outdated threshold, C uses the wrong initial vaccine pathway, and D incorrectly makes vaccination dependent on prior disease.
cueing_check: All four choices are parallel pneumococcal-vaccination pathways of comparable length and specificity; the prior uniquely-long correct answer and 'all/only' distractor wording were removed.
